correctness.rationale: The projective gradient is nonzero at points having at least three nonzero coordinates and zero at exactly the ten coordinate lines. In the chart x0=1, the Jacobian ideal at the coordinate vertex is generated by q_i=e2 of the other three y variables, because 3e3=∑y_iq_i and 1−y_i is a local unit. The reduced union ideal K=(y_i y_j) has six degree-two generators; the four q_i are linearly independent. Their 16 cubic multiples y_jq_i form a 16x16 matrix with exact determinant 48, computed by package check.py. Therefore mK⊂Q, K/Q has length 2 concentrated in degree 2 and m-annihilated; K²⊂Q. The same holds at five vertices and J=I elsewhere by invertible transverse Hessian. The sheaf exact sequence adds length 10 to HP 10d−5, yielding 10d+5. No finite enumeration is used for the universal proof.
